title: Lay out parts bins for a seated assembler
instruction: A worker sits at the far side of the bench, facing you, with both forearms resting on the bench. The pad between the worker's hands and you is the worker's reach zone. Set up the worker's station: put all three parts bins on the pad, standing upright and not stacked, with the heaviest bin nearest the worker's body and the lightest farthest from it, and at least 2 cm of clear space between bins. The bins hold the same parts, so a bigger bin is a heavier bin.
context: Bench layouts often place heavier supplies closer to the worker. This task applies that ordering rule using distance to a seated stand-in; the marked area is an enlarged proxy for a reach zone.
setup: World frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases (toward the worker), y to the robot's left, measured from the midpoint between the bases; heights from the table (bench) top, which is 760 mm above the floor; the table's far edge is at x = 910 mm. Worker stand-in (fixed, seated beyond the far edge, facing the arms, centred on y = -210 mm): a dark stool 340 mm across with its seat 450 mm above the floor, centred at (1050, -210); a grey torso block 220 mm deep (x 940-1160 mm, chest 30 mm clear of the table edge) and 360 mm wide (y -390 to -30 mm), from the stool seat to 300 mm above the bench top; a 200 mm skin-tone foam ball as the head, 5 mm above the torso; two skin-tone foam forearm blocks, 70 mm wide and 60 mm tall, lying flat on the bench from x = 530 mm out to the chest (x 935 mm), centred at y = -350 mm and y = -70 mm. Reach-zone pad (fixed, taped flat): a sheet of green 3 mm craft foam, 310 x 260 mm, spanning x 170-480 mm and y -340 to -80 mm (centred on the worker, 50 mm short of the forearm tips). Parts bins (loose, upright, positions are centres of the base): three closed, lidded small-parts boxes of the same blue polypropylene, each filled to the same density with the same parts (about 0.35 g per cubic cm of outside volume): large 180 x 64 x 75 mm tall, 300 g, at (300, 30) with its long side along x; medium 140 x 54 x 60 mm tall, 157 g, at (120, -210) with its long side along y; small 100 x 44 x 45 mm tall, 69 g, at (140, 20) with its long side along y. All three stand on the bench outside the pad (at least 23 mm clear of it).
scoring: Distances to the worker are measured horizontally from the middle of the worker's chest (x 940, y -210 mm) to the centre of a bin. A bin is on the pad when its centre, seen from above, is over the pad (x 170-480 mm, y -340 to -80 mm), its lowest point is at most 15 mm above the pad (not held, not on another bin) and it stands upright (its vertical axis within 20 degrees of vertical). If any bin is on the floor (centre below the bench top) or any bin rests on top of another (centre over another bin's footprint and bottom at or above that bin's top, less 10 mm), the score is 0. Otherwise: 0.15 for each bin on the pad; 0.15 for each of the three pairs (large-medium, medium-small, large-small) in which both bins are on the pad and the heavier one is at least 20 mm nearer the worker's chest; 0.10 if all three are on the pad and every two bins have at least 20 mm of clear space between them seen from above. Score = the sum (at most 1.0). So the start scores 0; one bin on the pad 0.15; two on the pad in the right order 0.45; all three on the pad in reverse order 0.55; all three with one neighbouring pair swapped 0.85; all three in order but touching 0.90; a stack of bins 0. Full success (1.0): all three upright on the pad, ordered heaviest nearest the worker, at least 20 mm apart, all at rest (under 1 cm/s) for 1 second. The score is taken at the end of the run.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the three bins back on their marked spots (tape crosses under each centre, with a tape line for the long side); the stand-in, forearms and pad stay fixed.
fidelity: Parts bins are approximated as closed boxes: each is one solid rigid box of one colour with its mass spread evenly (real counterparts: lidded parts boxes filled to the stated masses). Friction is rubber-like (1.2/1.0), higher than polypropylene on foam. The worker is a static stand-in. The reach zone is a fixed rectangle 460-770 mm from the chest, farther than a seated worker's normal reach, because the arms cannot reach the bench beside the worker; the task tests order by distance to the body.
